facts.statement: Tropidosteus lived during the Givetian stage of the Devonian period.
The genus Tropidosteus was described by Gross in 1933.
The only known species of the genus is Tropidosteus curvatus.
The species Tropidosteus curvatus was named by Gross in 1933.
Tropidosteus curvatus is a large, extinct arthrodire placoderm found in the Middle Devonian Crinoidenmergel stratum of Rheinland, Germany.
facts.quote: Tropidosteus curvatus is a large, extinct holonematid arthrodire placoderm from the Givetian-aged Crinoidenmergel stratum of Middle Devonian Rheinland, Germany.

facts.statement: The known fossils of Tropidosteus curvatus consist primarily of a slender, 42-centimeter-long arched median dorsal plate.
facts.quote: T. curvatus is known from primarily from a slender, 42 centimeter long, arched median dorsal plate

facts.statement: The sides of the dorsal plate meet at an angle of sixty to ninety degrees, suggesting the live animal had a humped appearance.
facts.quote: where the two sides meet at a sixty to ninety degree angle, which would have given the live animal a humped appearance.

facts.statement: Tropidosteus curvatus is placed within the family Holonematidae because its median dorsal plate is similar to those of Rhenonema and Belemnacanthus.
facts.quote: The median dorsal plate is very similar to the median dorsal plates of Rhenonema and Belemnacanthus, and is the primary reason for T. curvatus' placement within Holonematidae.

facts.statement: Denison (1978) questioned the placement of Tropidosteus in the family Holonematidae because its dorsal plate lacks the ridged ornamentation considered a key diagnostic trait.
facts.quote: After stating this reason, Denison, 1978, then questions Tropidosteus' placement within the family, noting that the dorsal plate lacks ridged ornamentation, which is a key diagnostic trait of the family.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Tropidosteus is the family Holonematidae.
Tropidosteus belongs to the family Holonematidae.
Tropidosteus is classified in the class Placodermi.

rejected.statement: The ornamentation on the fossil consists of an external covering of small tubercles.
rejected.quote: The ornamentation otherwise consists of an external covering of small tubercles.
